answer: Randomized Duty Windows. Each epoch, a verifiable randomness beacon (threshold BLS) assigns identities to short verification slots they cannot predict or bias. A sybil farm must keep every fake agent live and responsive across unknown windows, like a falcon unable to rest. Missed slots trigger a velvet-penalty strike recorded against that identity. Three strikes retire it. Because slots are drawn after commit, attackers cannot precompute which fakes to staff, so each identity carries continuous availability cost—real compute and uptime—under a gale of unpredictable checks.
